Cleaning Environment
```{r}
rm(list=ls())
```

```{r loadlib, results='hide', message=F, warning=F}
library(zoo)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(rcompanion)
library(here)
```

```{r reading data}
demographic <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/dog_profile.csv"))
labs <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/clinical_labs.csv"))
physical <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/exam_physical.csv"))

labs_wbc <- subset(labs, test_name == "WBC")

physical_weight <- subset(physical, complete.cases(weight))

demographic %<>% subset(subject_id %in% physical_weight$subject_id & subject_id %in% labs_wbc$subject_id)

nrow(demographic)
```

```{r clean demographic}
# Event type for censoring. TRUE = death, False = all other outcomes
demographic$event_type <- demographic$death_date != ""

# Reduce all event dates to a single column
demographic <- unite(demographic, withdrawn_date, inactive_date, death_date, sep = "") %>% rename(event_date = withdrawn_date)

# If no other event date, include date when data released.
# This would represent the last follow-up, since the demographic data is released with no embargo.
demographic$event_date %<>% sub(pattern = "^$", replacement = "2025-01")

# Convert to year-month date type to allow for numeric operations
demographic$birth_date %<>% as.yearmon()
demographic$event_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Determine age at event (in years)
demographic$event_age <-demographic$event_date - demographic$birth_date

# Clean up, keep only relevant variables
demographic %<>% select(subject_id, sex_status, birth_date, event_date, event_age, event_type) %>%
  na.omit()
```

```{r cleaning weight and WBC}
# Remove all non-weight variables (and remove any incomplete entries)
physical_weight %<>% select(subject_id, record_date, weight) %>%
  rename(weight_date = record_date) %>%
  subset(weight_date != "") %>%
  na.omit()

# Convert to year-month date type
physical_weight$weight_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Merge with demographic to determine age (in years) at record date
physical_weight %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, birth_date, sex_status), by = "subject_id")
physical_weight$weight_age <- physical_weight$weight_date - physical_weight$birth_date
physical_weight$sex_status %<>% as.factor()

physical_weight <- physical_weight[physical_weight$weight < 200,]

# Remove all non-WBC variables (and remove any incomplete entries)
labs_wbc %<>% select(subject_id, visit_date, test_value) %>%
  rename(WBC_date = visit_date, WBC = test_value) %>%
  subset(WBC_date != "")
labs_wbc$WBC %<>% as.numeric()
labs_wbc %<>% na.omit()

# Convert to year-month date type
labs_wbc$WBC_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Merge with demographic to determine age (in years) at record date
labs_wbc %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, birth_date, sex_status), by = "subject_id")
labs_wbc$WBC_age <- labs_wbc$WBC_date - labs_wbc$birth_date
labs_wbc$sex_status %<>% as.factor()

# Remove extreme WBC (likely data entry error)
labs_wbc <- labs_wbc[labs_wbc$WBC < 100,]
```

```{r basic summary}
print("WBC mean, median, range:")
mean(labs_wbc$WBC)
median(labs_wbc$WBC)
range(labs_wbc$WBC)
hist(labs_wbc[labs_wbc$WBC < 20,]$WBC)
qqnorm(labs_wbc$WBC)
```

```{r}
labs_wbc$WBC_Blom <- blom(labs_wbc$WBC)

```

```{r}
wbc_age_smooth <- ggplot(labs_wbc, aes(x = WBC_age, y = WBC)) +
  geom_smooth()
wbc_age_smooth

wbc_sex_age_smooth <- ggplot(subset(labs_wbc, sex_status %in% c("Spayed Female", "Neutered Male")), aes(x = WBC_age, y = WBC, color = sex_status)) +
  geom_smooth()
wbc_sex_age_smooth
```

Let's try and do the same LME as we did for RDW.

```{r Determining PLL}
# Create a new dataframe with only labs for dogs that aren't censored
labs_wbc_dead <- labs_wbc[labs_wbc$subject_id %in% demographic[which(demographic$event_type), "subject_id"],]

# Merge with demographic to get age at death
labs_wbc_dead %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, event_age), by = "subject_id")

# Divide age at wbc by age at death to determine percentage of life lived at wbc
labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL <- labs_wbc_dead$WBC_age / labs_wbc_dead$event_age

print("PLL at WBC labs mean, median, range:")
mean(labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL)
median(labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL)
range(labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL)
hist(labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL)
qqnorm(labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL)
qqline(labs_wbc_dead$WBC_PLL)

```

```{r Initial LME}
library(nlme)

#age_sex_lme <- lme(WBC_Blom ~ WBC_age + sex_status, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = labs_wbc)
#the above gave an error
age_sex_lme <- lme(WBC_Blom ~ WBC_age + sex_status, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = labs_wbc, control = lmeControl(opt = "optim"))
summary(age_sex_lme)


PLL_sex_lme  <- lme(WBC_Blom ~ WBC_PLL + sex_status, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = labs_wbc_dead)
summary(PLL_sex_lme)
```

```{r Predict PLL}
WBC_sex_lme  <- lme(WBC_PLL ~ WBC_Blom + sex_status, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = labs_wbc_dead)
summary(WBC_sex_lme)
```


We want to determine if it's alright to combine sexes. Let's look at an ANOVA of WBC on sex/status.

```{r WBC sex/status ANOVA}
# Fit one-way ANOVA and report results
wbc_sex_anova <- aov(WBC_Blom ~ sex_status, labs_wbc_dead)
summary(wbc_sex_anova)

# Diagnostic plots for our ANOVA, ensuring residuals are normally distributed
qqnorm(residuals(wbc_sex_anova))
qqline(residuals(wbc_sex_anova))
plot(wbc_sex_anova, which = 1)

# Tukey pairwise comparison
TukeyHSD(wbc_sex_anova)

ggplot(labs_wbc, aes(x = sex_status, y = WBC_Blom)) + geom_boxplot()
```

This would seem to suggest that there is a significant difference between neutered males and spayed females, at least in terms of mean WBC. However, I wonder if this is accounted for by any differences in lifespan, age at testing, etc. Let's see if this sex difference has a significant effect on our PLL-corrected LME.

```{r Predict PLL}
WBC_sex_fixed_lme  <- lme(WBC_PLL ~ WBC_Blom + sex_status, random = ~ 1|subject_id, data = subset(labs_wbc_dead, sex_status %in% c("Spayed Female", "Neutered Male")))
summary(WBC_sex_fixed_lme)
```

This result indicates to me that it would be appropriate to combine the sexes when plotting against PLL, so long as we don't include intact animals and clearly report sex effects on unadjusted age (as they did have significant differences in the previous LME).

```{r WBC PLL Smooth plot}
wbc_pll_smooth <- ggplot(labs_wbc_dead, aes(x = WBC_PLL, y = WBC)) +
  geom_smooth()
wbc_pll_smooth


wbc_sex_pll_smooth <- ggplot(subset(labs_wbc_dead, sex_status %in% c("Spayed Female", "Neutered Male")), aes(x = WBC_PLL, y = WBC, color = sex_status)) +
  geom_smooth()
wbc_sex_pll_smooth

# Matching colors to our other graphs
wbc_sex_pll_smooth + scale_colour_manual(values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"))

```

Use only records included in the RDW analysis
```{r Subset to records with RDW}
labs_rdw <- subset(labs, test_name == "RDW")
labs_rdw %<>% select(subject_id, visit_date, test_value) %>%
  rename(RDW_date = visit_date, RDW = test_value) %>%
  subset(RDW_date != "")
labs_rdw$RDW %<>% as.numeric()
labs_rdw %<>% na.omit()
labs_rdw$RDW_date %<>% as.yearmon()

labs_wbc_dead_filtered <- semi_join(labs_wbc_dead, labs_rdw, by = join_by(subject_id, WBC_date == RDW_date))
```

```{r Create subset plot}
ggplot(subset(labs_wbc_dead_filtered, sex_status %in% c("Spayed Female", "Neutered Male")), aes(x = WBC_PLL, y = WBC, color = sex_status)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"))
```
